newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BENFICA BID TO REIN IN RUNAWAY PORTO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BENFICA BID TO REIN IN RUNAWAY PORTO.

text.p: Benfica face Porto on Saturday knowing it could be their last real chance to stop the reigning champions running away with a record third successive Portuguese league title.
The "Reds" are in second spot in the league but five points adrift of Porto and a home defeat could end any hopes they still have of overhauling their great northern rivals.
The significance is underlined by the fact that only one other team -- Lisbon's Sporting -- have won the Portuguese championship in the past 20 years and that was 15 years ago.

"With so many games still to play, you cannot say defeat will decide the title. But I have to admit that if we lose...things will get more difficult," Benfica's Brazilian coach Paulo Autuori told journalists.

A season's best crowd of 70,000 is expected at Lisbon's Stadium of Light for the match, with extra police being drafted in for fear of clashes between two of the most vociferous sets of supporters in the country.

The counter-punching Porto are expected to field three central defenders, adopting the defensive strategy that has proved so successful this season not just in domestic but also in European competitions.
Porto, whose path to the quarter-finals of the European Cup included a historic 3-2 defeat of AC Milan in the San Siro stadium, have yet to taste defeat in any competition this season.
But Benfica, still smarting from a 5-0 drubbing at the hands of Porto in the Portuguese Supercup in September, enjoy nothing better than puncturing Porto's pride.
They did it last season when they ended a 53-match unbeaten run by the northerners with a determined 2-1 home victory, even if the win did nothing to change the course of the championship.
Ironically for a clash so important to the Portuguese, the match has a highly Brazilian flavour.

Porto are likely to field three Brazilian strikers, with the lanky Mario Jardel, the league's top scorer in his first season, probably posing the greatest threat to Michel Preud'homme, Benfica's veteran goalkeeper.

Benfica's midfield is marshalled by Brazilians Valdo Filho and Alexandre Amaral, while countryman Osmar Donizete, together with club captain and Portuguese international Joao Vieira Pinto, provides much of the attacking flair.
Autuori is expected to field an attacking formation but he has yet to decide whether to field Swedish striker Martin Pringle.
After a slow start, Pringle finally came good last weekend when he scored twice -- his first goals of the season -- in Benfica's 5-1 defeat of Leca.
Benfica - Michel Preud'Homme, Jose Calado, Jorge Soares, Jorge Bermudez, Pedro Henriques, Alexandre Amaral, Valdo Filho, Glenn Helder, Joao Pinto, Osmar Donizete, Martin Pringle.
Porto - Henrique Hilario, Paulinho Santos, Fernando Mendes, Aloisio Alves, Jorge Costa, Jose Barroso, Zlatko Zahovic, Ljubimnko Drulovic, Edmilson Pimenta, Mario Jardel, Artur Oliveira.
